Aether splits the ClientHello of the MASQUE HTTP/2 carrier into small pieces with a delay between them, so a firewall that resets a whole ClientHello whose SNI ends in cloudflareclient.com does not see one. Implemented in aether/src/fragment.rs.
Off by default in Aether. Applies to the HTTP/2 carrier only, never to QUIC or WireGuard, so turning it on also selects that carrier.
n or a-b, for example 16-32 (the Aether default)
n or a-b, for example 2-10 (the Aether default)

AETHER_MASQUE_H2_FRAGMENT_SNI: put the split in the middle of the SNI host name instead of at a random offset. Upstream has no CLI flag for it, so it reaches Aether only through this app\u2019s bridge.
Applied — this route runs MASQUE over HTTP/2
Off — this route runs MASQUE over HTTP/3 (QUIC)

Turning fragmenting on switches this route\u2019s MASQUE carrier from HTTP/3 (QUIC) to HTTP/2 (TCP), because the fragments are written into that carrier\u2019s TLS ClientHello (aether/src/masque_h2.rs). The scan and the tunnel both follow the carrier, so nothing is left half applied.
Fragmenting needs the MASQUE transport: Aether applies it only on the MASQUE-over-HTTP/2 carrier. It is unavailable while this route uses %1$s.
Fragmenting saved with the route; Aether applies it on the next start.
Fragmenting saved; Aether is restarting with it.

One carrier only: MASQUE over HTTP/2. It never applies to the HTTP/3 (QUIC) MASQUE path, and never to WireGuard, gool or mim. This app selects that carrier for you when fragmenting is on, and selects QUIC again when it is off.

These values are stored with the route, appear in its exported JSON, and are written into the engine\u2019s environment before each start — Aether reads them per connection (aether/src/fragment.rs).

Resolved inside the app private directory and sent to aether_identity_open.
Applied for MASQUE only: ffi::job_ech returns no key for WireGuard, which has no TLS handshake to hide a name in.

Applied to the scan (noize::from_profile) and to a WireGuard tunnel (aethernoize::from_profile), but not to a MASQUE tunnel, which reads its profile from AETHER_NOIZE — a variable this path cannot set. The two parsers also differ: the scan has no balanced case, so balanced scans as firewall.
The team name is sent, but enrolment also needs a service token or a one-time code. The aether_team_* calls are wired in AetherBridge and are not used by this screen yet.

Aether reads this from its own environment (set by the CLI). No field for it exists on aether_tunnel_start, and Android has no public API for setting the process environment, so the value is saved and shown but not applied.
Only the aether_core_start CLI flow acts on this; the identity/scan/tunnel path this build uses has no field for it.

Written into the engine\u2019s environment before each start (AETHER_MASQUE_HTTP2 and AETHER_MASQUE_H2_FRAGMENT*), which is where Aether reads it — aether_tunnel_start has no field for it. One carrier only: MASQUE over HTTP/2, so enabling it switches this route away from QUIC. A blank size or delay leaves Aether\u2019s own default in place.
Applied through the same call, as AETHER_MASQUE_H2_FRAGMENT_SNI. Upstream has no --fragment-sni flag, so this is the only way it reaches Aether, and it only matters on the HTTP/2 carrier.
Needs a Tor or Psiphon component that is not bundled with this build, and this path forwards no Tor or Psiphon setting.

Aether is driven step by step through aether_identity_open, aether_scan_start and aether_tunnel_start, so the scan\u2019s chosen endpoint and every failure are reported as they happen. Only what those payloads carry is applied.

Aether is started with its own command line (aether_core_start). This is the only path that applies gool, masquerade-in-masquerade, Tor and Psiphon layering, Zero Trust, routing rules, the upstream proxy, the in-tunnel DNS list, quick reconnect, traffic statistics and the socket mark.
Chosen per route. The full-engine path is the only one that applies every setting below; the scan-then-tunnel path reports each step instead.
Stored with this route, applied only on the full-engine start path: %1$s
Applied: the full-engine path runs Aether\u2019s own command line (aether_core_start), which sets this variable before the engine starts.

Applied on the full-engine path. Psiphon itself needs the psiphon-tunnel-core child process, which this build ships when the build produced it; without it the start is refused with that reason instead of failing inside the engine.

Applied on the full-engine path. Tor needs a pluggable transport only for bridges that name one (obfs4, snowflake, webtunnel); this build ships lyrebird for those, and plain Tor needs no child process at all.
Every remaining flag the Aether core accepts, modelled one-to-one against aether/src/cli.rs. They apply on the full-engine start path.
